Task: Design de novo protein binders for the human TREM2 IgSF domain.
Target the V-type Ig-like extracellular domain of human TREM2 (PDB 5ELI, ~15 kDa, β-sandwich with CDR-like loops at the ligand-binding apex). Aim binders at the IgSF domain to stabilize TREM2 on the cell surface — mimic the VHB937 mechanism, NOT the stalk-binding AL002 mechanism that triggers internalization. The stalk region (res 133–172) is absent from 5ELI, so ignore it.
5ELI construct sequence (IgSF domain + C-terminal His-tag): TGHNTTVFQGVAGQSLQVSCPYDSMKHWGRRKAWCRQLGEKGPCQRVVSTHNLWLLSFLRRWNGSTAITDDTLGGTLTITLRNLQPHDAGLYQCQSLHGSEADTLRKVLVEVLADPLGTKHHHHHH

Hard constraints:
* Each sequence ≤ 250 amino acids
* Ranking metric is ipSAE; optimize for it
* Experimental validation is BLI binding affinity, so favor designs likely to fold and bind in vitro (sane pLDDT, low interface PAE, reasonable expression/solubility)

Note: I want a IPSAE atleast above an .88

1	# NOTES.md — Cross-session engineering notebook
2	
3	**Purpose:** persistent log of fixes, gotchas, pinned versions, and decisions the next session needs and that aren't in PRD / ARCHITECTURE / PLAN / README / CLAUDE / git log. Assume the reader has zero memory of prior sessions.
4	
5	**Convention:** **append-only between compactions** — don't rewrite past entries; strike through with `~~text~~` + a follow-up if something proves wrong. The repo owner may periodically **compact** this file (prune stale/superseded entries, tighten verbose ones); the full pre-compaction history always remains in git. Active debugging lives in `DEBUG.md` and moves here once resolved. Per-entry: what triggered it · the fact the next person needs · why it matters · links (commit / file:line).
6	
7	> **Compacted 2026-05-26** (owner-directed). Removed superseded strike-through entries (Gemini→Claude migration, RFdiffusion v1), one-off "phase landed" status notes, a stale in-progress-run handoff, and verbose E2E numbers. Recover anything via `git log -p NOTES.md`.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Tooling & environment
12	
13	### Fresh Lambda VM bring-up (bare Ubuntu 24.04, NOT Lambda Stack)
14	Lambda VMs have come up as **bare Ubuntu 24.04** with NO driver/Docker (SETUP.md's "pre-installed" claim is false). Install order, all noninteractive:
15	1. `sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive NEEDRESTART_MODE=a apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-580-server nvidia-utils-580-server` (580 = stable, CUDA 12/13; avoids the debconf whiptail under non-tty).
16	2. `sudo modprobe nvidia nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm` — no reboot; DKMS builds against the running kernel (6.8.0-62). `nvidia-smi` may say "couldn't communicate" until modprobe fully loads — retry after.
17	3. `sudo apt-get install -y docker.io` + `sudo usermod -aG docker ubuntu`.
18	4. NVIDIA Container Toolkit from the upstream apt repo (gpgkey `nvidia.github.io/libnvidia-container/gpgkey`) → `sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=docker && sudo systemctl restart docker`.
19	5. Verify: `sudo docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base-ubuntu22.04 nvidia-smi`.
20	
21	**Docker-group footgun:** `usermod -aG docker` does NOT propagate into the shell/session that ran it. `proteinclaw`'s LocalRunner calls `docker` directly, so wrap every invocation: `sg docker -c 'bash -c "source .venv/bin/activate && proteinclaw ..."'`. A fresh SSH login picks up the group and doesn't need this.
22	
23	**Persistent FS:** wire the §2 symlinks (`~/.cache/{huggingface,rfdiffusion,proteinmpnn,openfold}` + `~/.proteinclaw` → `/lambda/nfs/<name>/...`) BEFORE any weight download. Mount name varies per account (seen: `Daanish2`, `Daanishfiles`). Comes back empty on a fresh VM → all weights + Docker images rebuild (~30–60 min cold).
24	
25	### 2026-06-07 bring-up: full recipe reproduced clean; nvidia-container-toolkit 1.19.1
26	Re-ran the entire bare-Ubuntu §"Fresh Lambda VM bring-up" on this box from scratch (A10, no driver/docker/uv at start, OAuth creds + node v22.22.3 + claude already present). Everything matched the 2026-06-06 entry: driver **580.159.03**, docker **29.1.3**, `modprobe nvidia nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm` (no reboot), GPU passthrough into `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base` OK. New version pin worth recording: **nvidia-container-toolkit 1.19.1** (libnvidia-container 1.19.1). uv **0.11.19**, venv on python 3.12.3, `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"` clean, **325 host tests pass** (`-m "not gpu"`), `proteinclaw 0.1.0` CLI works. `doctor` = all **PASS** (note: weights showed PASS not WARN — the `~/.cache/{huggingface,rfdiffusion,proteinmpnn,openfold}` dirs already existed/were created as plain dirs on the local disk; no Lambda NFS here). **Docker-group footgun confirmed:** the shell that ran `usermod -aG docker` does NOT get the group — ran `doctor` via `sg docker -c 'bash -c "source .venv/bin/activate && proteinclaw ..."'`; a fresh SSH login won't need the wrapper. Weights NOT yet downloaded (lazy, will hit the 1.3 TB local disk on first run). GPU tool Docker images NOT yet built (LocalRunner builds them on first `proteinclaw run`).
27	
28	### 2026-06-06 bring-up: node v22 + driver 580.159.03 (CUDA 13.0) both work
29	Ran the full bare-Ubuntu §"Fresh Lambda VM bring-up" recipe on this box (A10, no driver/docker/uv at start). Two deviations from the pinned versions, both fine: **node was v22.22.3** (not the pinned 20.x) and **claude-agent-sdk works against it**; `nvidia-driver-580-server` came up as **580.159.03 reporting CUDA 13.0**, GPU passthrough into `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-base` container OK, `doctor` all PASS (weights WARN = expected, lazy). No reboot needed (modprobe). Docker 29.1.3. This box has **no Lambda NFS** — `~/.cache/*` weight symlinks (§2) were NOT wired; weights will land on the local 1.3 TB disk.
30	
31	### GPU is an A10 (24 GB) reporting 22 GB — sits exactly on the floor
32	`lspci` shows `GA102GL [A10]`; `nvidia-smi` reports **23028 MiB**, and `total_gb = 23028 // 1024 = 22`. The global VRAM floor was lowered 24→22 (commit `b5e222d`, in `doctor.py` `GLOBAL_VRAM_FLOOR_GB` + RFD3/AF2 `tool.yaml`) for exactly this card, so doctor reads "22 GB ≥ 22 GB floor → PASS". **Do NOT lower floors further** — a lower floor doesn't add memory, it just removes the OOM guardrail (violates "fail loud"). AF2-multimer on large binder+target complexes (>~400 aa) is the tightest step on 22 GB; fix OOM with a smaller binder / fewer recycles, not a lower floor.
33	
34	### Pinned versions that matter
35	`nvidia-driver-580-server`, `docker.io` (24.04 default) + `nvidia-container-toolkit`, `python3.12`, `uv 0.11.16`, `node 20.x`, `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`, `claude-agent-sdk 0.2.87`. Per-model image pins are in the Tool-wrapper section below.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Tool wrappers (4-file convention + `_normalize.py`)
40	
41	### Shared LocalRunner mechanics (apply to every GPU tool)
42	- **Container UID/GID:** `docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g)` so workspace artifacts aren't root-owned. Tool Dockerfiles must NOT set a restrictive `USER` (would block reading the bind-mounted entrypoint).
43	- **Weight caches mount at `/cache/<name>`** (not `/root/.cache`, which UID 1000 can't write). Each tool's Dockerfile sets its env (`HF_HOME=/cache/huggingface`, etc.) + `mkdir -p /cache/<name>`.
44	- **Build context staging:** `_ensure_image` copies the tool dir + `_SHARED_BUILD_FILES` (`_gpu_metrics.py`) into a tempdir so Dockerfiles can `COPY _gpu_metrics.py` (no path-traversal in build context). Add new shared helpers there.
45	- **Path translation:** `_translate_workspace_paths` rewrites `/workspace/...` in result envelopes → host paths. Containers tagged `--label proteinclaw.session=<sid>` (used by `proteinclaw cancel`).
46	- **`_normalize.py` per tool** (the allowed 5th file): parameter/PDB normalisation extracted so host-side tests import it without container-only imports. Tests MUST load it via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location` under a **unique** module name — plain `from _normalize import` collides across tools in one pytest session.
47	
48	### Conditional JSON-Schema (`allOf`/`if`/`then`/`else`) in a tool.yaml silently DROPS the tool from the agent (2026-06-07)
49	**Symptom:** run `b269b01802e5` made **0 RFD3 calls** and the agent's plan.md said *"RFdiffusion3 … was not loaded in this session's deferred-tools list"* — it reused prior backbones instead. The immediately-prior run `a89c4dfe5a89` (before the edit) called RFD3 fine. **Root cause:** I had added an `allOf: [{if/then/else}]` block to RFD3's `tool.yaml` to make `required` conditional (de-novo vs partial mode). The registry's `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` *accepts* it, and `build_mcp_server` builds fine — but the agent runs under the **`claude_code` system-prompt preset** (`core._build_options`), which uses **deferred tools / ToolSearch** and sends each tool's schema as an **Anthropic tool `input_schema`**. The API tool-schema validator does **NOT** support `allOf`/`if`/`then`/`else`/`oneOf`/`anyOf` — so RFD3's schema was rejected and the tool silently vanished from the agent's loadable set (every other tool has a flat schema and survived). **Fix:** reverted RFD3 to a flat schema (no `required`, no `allOf`); the two modes are enforced at runtime by `normalize_args`/`normalize_partial_args`, NOT jsonschema (runtime args are never jsonschema-validated — confirmed: `router.route`→`runner.run` does no schema validation). **Rule: keep every `tool.yaml` `parameters` schema FLAT** — type/properties/required/enum/min/max/pattern only; no conditional keywords, or the tool disappears from the agent under the claude_code preset. tool.yaml is host-read by the registry (NOT baked into the image) so schema fixes need no rebuild.
50	
51	### RFD3 partial diffusion: `partial_t` is Angstroms, NOT timesteps (2026-06-07, GPU-verified)
52	RFD3 **does** support partial diffusion, but the param is `partial_t` = **Angstroms of noise** (RFD3 caps ≤15; field in `rfd3/inference/input_parsing.py`), NOT the classic RFdiffusion `partial_T` timestep count. The old skill refs to `partial_T=20`/`T=50` were wrong on both name-semantics and value (would've been a near-cold-start, and the wrapper never exposed any such param so the call would 404). Now wired into the wrapper: new params `start_pdb` (a prior binder+target complex under /workspace) + `partial_t` + `binder_chain`/`target_chain`; switches `run()` to `normalize_partial_args` + a contig-free `build_input_spec` branch (`{dialect:2, input:start_pdb, partial_t, is_non_loopy}` — RFD3 forbids `length`/contig with partial_t and re-noises the WHOLE complex "without constraints", target included). tool.yaml uses `allOf/if-then-else` to require `start_pdb` when `partial_t` present, else `target_pdb`+`hotspot_residues` (Draft202012 supports it; note: **call-args are NOT jsonschema-validated at runtime** — only `normalize_*` + RFD3 `prevalidate_inputs` enforce; schema is planner-facing). **Footgun: the image bakes `_normalize.py`/`implementation.py` via `COPY`, and `_ensure_image` only builds when the image is MISSING — so after editing wrapper code you MUST manually rebuild** (`docker build -t proteinclaw/rfdiffusion3:0.1.0 <staged ctx with _gpu_metrics.py>`), or delete the image. GPU-verified on run-29d's rank-1 complex (`partial_t=5`): 2 backbones, binder A=96/target B=112 preserved, first CA shifted ~0.6 Å (genuine local refinement). 28 normalize tests + skills check green. Skill now PREFERS partial diffusion as the first round-2 refinement (2-6 Å polish, 8-12 Å explore).
53	
54	### ProteinMPNN `use_soluble_model` added; soluble_model_weights/ ships ALL FOUR models (2026-06-07, GPU-verified)
55	Wired a new flat boolean param `use_soluble_model` into the ProteinMPNN wrapper (`_normalize.py` passthrough, `implementation.py:_build_argv` switches `--path_to_model_weights` to `/opt/ProteinMPNN/soluble_model_weights`, `tool.yaml` flat boolean default false). soluble_mpnn is the literature default for de-novo binders (Bennett 2023/BindCraft — fewer apolar exposed residues). **Footgun corrected mid-task:** the dauparas/ProteinMPNN GitHub README lists soluble weights for only `v_48_010`/`v_48_020`, so I first added a `SOLUBLE_MODELS` validation rejecting v_48_002/v_48_030 under soluble. **That was wrong** — the actual `git clone --depth 1` HEAD baked into the image ships **all four** `.pt` files in `soluble_model_weights/` (verified: `docker run --entrypoint ls ... /opt/ProteinMPNN/soluble_model_weights` → v_48_002/010/020/030.pt). Removed the restriction; `use_soluble_model` now works with any allowed model. **Lesson: verify weight availability against the actual built image, not the upstream README** — the README was stale. GPU-verified both `v_48_020` and `v_48_002` under soluble on run b269b01802e5's rank-1 backbone (chain A binder): both produced sequences, no error, ~470 MB VRAM peak. The image had to be built fresh here anyway (none existed); for an existing box, editing wrapper code needs a manual rebuild (same `COPY`-bakes footgun as the RFD3 entry above). 14 normalize tests + 27 skills check green.
56	
57	### Per-model dep pins (load-bearing — don't modernize)
58	- **ProteinMPNN:** torch 2.4.1 cu121 on CUDA 12.4 base; bundled vanilla weights. `fix_positions` NOT implemented. Literature default for de-novo binders is `soluble_mpnn` (not yet wrapped — add `use_soluble_model`).
59	- **ESMFold:** `facebook/esmfold_v1` via HF transformers; **torch==2.6.0** cu124 required (CVE-2025-32434 — older torch refuses `from_pretrained`). ~14.2 GB VRAM. >1024 aa rejected at normalize.
60	- **RFD3:** `rc-foundry[rfd3]` on base `rosettacommons/foundry:slim`; `HOME=/tmp`+`XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/.cache`. Checkpoint via `foundry install rfd3` → `~/.cache/rfdiffusion`. Canonical ckpt URL `files.ipd.uw.edu/pub/rfd3/rfd3_foundry_2025_12_01_remapped.ckpt`. **Patch `/app/foundry/.env`** (sed) to prepend `/cache/rfdiffusion` to `FOUNDRY_CHECKPOINT_DIRS` — dotenv loads at runtime and overrides a plain `ENV`. Outputs `.cif.gz` (atom14 mmCIF) → wrapper auto-converts to PDB via biotite. Hotspots are per-atom (`{A56:"CB,CG"}`); wrapper defaults each residue to `CA,CB` (Gly→`CA`).
61	- **AF2-multimer (ColabFold):** base `nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda:12.2.2-cudnn8-...` — **MUST be cuDNN 8** (CUDA 12.4 ships cuDNN 9 → jax rejects). `colabfold[alphafold]==1.5.5`, `jax[cuda12]==0.4.23` (0.4.24+ removed `jax.linear_util`), `numpy<2`, `MPLCONFIGDIR=/tmp/matplotlib`. OpenFold params (~5 GB) lazy-download on first call. `complex_confidence` = mean binder-chain CA pLDDT = the ranking signal.
62	
63	### ipSAE interface metrics in the AF2 envelope
64	Dunbrack's `ipsae.py` (MIT, numpy-only) fetched into the image at build, **pinned to SHA `6174cf9e71cb1bd660cc805856a18c4871a6dec3`** (`IPSAE_SHA` ARG). `_compute_ipsae` derives `ipsae/iptm/pdockq/pdockq2/lis` from the rank-1 PAE matrix (`*_scores_rank_001_*.json`). ipSAE is **derived, not a ColabFold field**; output txt cutoffs are zero-padded 2-char (`5`→`05`); ipSAE is asymmetric (surface the `Type==max` row). **Soft-fail by design:** scorer failure → structure still returns, `ipsae=null` + `ipsae_error`. Ranking still sorts by `complex_confidence`; ipSAE/iptm are advisory (`ipsae ≳ 0.3` plausible). DB schema v1→v2 added `ipsae/iptm/pdockq/lis`. **STILL OPEN:** the AF2 image's `RUN wget` ipSAE layer is unverified in-container on GPU here — rebuild `proteinclaw/af2multimer:0.1.0` + one AF2 call before trusting it.
65	
66	---
67	
68	## Plain-Python tools (data + research)
69	
70	Shared layer: `tools/_http.py` (UA + timeouts) and `tools/_paths.py` (session workspace + per-host cache) — reuse, don't roll your own `requests`. Note: PRD §9.1's `web.py` (DuckDuckGo) was **never built** — general web search is the SDK's built-in WebFetch/WebSearch.
71	
72	- **UniProt:** `recommendedName.fullName.value` is the formal name (e.g. "Programmed cell death 1 ligand 1"), NOT the alias ("PD-L1"). Aliases under `alternativeNames` are not extracted in v1 — footgun for exact-match callers.
73	- **PDB:** `_filter_pdb` matches TER records by their own chain id (col 22), not a trailing-state flag — otherwise a discarded chain's TER leaks and naive parsers (PyMOL/Biopython) mis-read residue ranges.
74	- **`data.pdb_fetch` counts ordered waters/HETATM as chain residues.** 1UBQ chain A reports "134 residues, no gaps" but only 1-76 are protein; 77-134 are waters. `gaps: []` does NOT mean the whole range is protein — verify the true protein span (last `^ATOM` residue) before cropping. (This is the lesson the agent itself recorded in `skills/learned/target-resolution.md`.)
75	- **Literature/PubMed rate-limits:** a 429 → `{rate_limited: true, results: []}` is correct degradation (PRD §10.2), NOT a tool bug. `research.{literature_search,pubmed_search}` are single-query (NCBI throttled the old parallel path).
76	- **RCSB Search API:** response key is `result_set` (underscore); per-entry metadata (resolution/date/method) needs a 2nd Data-API pass (`data.rcsb.org/rest/v1/core/entry/{id}`).
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Agent core & skill file
81	
82	### Auth: OAuth via `claude login`, NOT `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (the trap)
83	The Agent SDK reads OAuth from `~/.claude/.credentials.json` → subscription billing automatically. **If `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set it silently wins**, billing pay-as-you-go while you think you're on subscription. `doctor.check_claude_auth` is 4-state (OAuth=PASS, OAuth+key=WARN-trap, key-only=PASS-api, neither=FAIL). `~/.proteinclaw/config.toml` holds model selection only — no secrets. Unset the key + `sed -i '/ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/d' ~/.bashrc`.
84	
85	### Research fan-out + the scout-refusal finding (hard-won, A/B-verified)
86	Scouts are read-only `research` (Sonnet) / `research_pro` (Opus escalation) subagents in `core.py:_research_agents()`. **The runtime spawn tool is `"Agent"`, NOT `"Task"`** — `_build_options` allows both; under `bypassPermissions` the `allowed_tools` list is documentation, not enforcement (verify tool names from a real trace). Key finding: Sonnet's safety classifier **refuses immune-checkpoint interface/residue queries at the TOPIC level — rephrasing/context does NOT help** (2×2 A/B: sonnet+PD-L1-residues REFUSED, opus+same OK, both fine on benign targets). Opus only helps with pure-retrieval framing (no design-intent line, no drug brand names). **Robust fix = ROUTING, not fighting the filter:** determine hotspots via the main agent's own `Bash` structural sandbox (contact/BSA on the co-crystal PDB) — reliable, zero refusals, more accurate; point scouts only at filter-safe topics (prior campaigns, fold designability, length/topology, developability). The propose→challenge(DEFEND)→adjudicate→converge debate mechanic is **verified firing** (e.g. TREM2 run `6e8c60a78622`: 6 scouts incl. 2 DEFEND, the agent overturned an epitope hypothesis on cited evidence). A dedicated `analysis.interface_residues` MCP tool (hotspots never touch an LLM) is the clean long-term fix.
87	
88	### Agent stops early + mis-narrates round count (2026-06-06)
89	Two related findings on the TREM2 runs. (1) **The agent narrated "stopped at round 2 of 4" on runs that were launched with `--rounds 1`** (`run_started.rounds==1` is authoritative; both `adbe5874aeb4` and `29d98715cdb4` were rounds=1). With rounds=1 the budget addendum says "1 round, run pipeline once" — the agent did an internal broad-then-focused MPNN re-sample within the single round and invented the "/4" frame. Lesson: trust `run_started.rounds` in the trace, not the agent's prose, for the actual cap. (2) **Even when told to iterate, the agent bailed early** citing "diminishing returns / same geometric constraint / no new hypothesis." Tightened both `_rounds_addendum` (capped multi-round branch in `core.py`) and `skills/proteindesign.md` §Self-refining loop with a **hard "do NOT stop early while gate unmet and budget remains" rule** + a structurally-distinct-pivot ladder (new topology/epitope/length regime) so "no new idea" → *generate one*, never finalize. Early finalize is now permitted ONLY when the gate is met (≥3 hits). `test_rounds.py` (8) + `skills check` (27) green. Note: the ipSAE 0.93 gate is unreachable (best observed 0.82), so with this change a capped run will now spend its full budget every time — intended, per owner.
90	
91	### `run_started` trace ALWAYS logged rounds=1 — logging bug, now fixed (2026-06-07)
92	`TraceWriter.run_started` has `rounds: int = 1` default and `core.py` called it WITHOUT passing rounds (`_drive` never even received it) → **every** run's `run_started` event logged `"rounds": 1` regardless of the real `--rounds` flag. This silently misled diagnosis (I repeatedly concluded "you passed --rounds 1" from the trace when the user had passed 4). The real cap lives only in the `_rounds_addendum` text the agent sees + `effective_max_turns`. Fixed: threaded `rounds` through `run_campaign`→`_drive`→`run_started`. **To know a run's actual round budget, do NOT trust pre-fix traces' `rounds` field** — infer from RFD3 call count / plan.md round narration instead. (Run `5707e91b52df` logged rounds=1 but genuinely ran 4 rounds incl. 2 partial-diffusion refinements.)
93	
94	### Confirmation pass (num_models=5) is a ROBUSTNESS test, not a score-lifter (2026-06-07)
95	Empirical from run `5707e91b52df` round 4: re-scoring top-6 at num_models=5/num_recycle=8 left ipSAE ≈ unchanged or slightly LOWER for 5/6 solid designs (delta -0.02..0.0), and **collapsed** the 6th (triage 0.828 → confirmed 0.635 — a lucky single-model outlier). So the pass catches false positives; it does NOT lift a real design's ipSAE. The earlier skill claim "ensembled ipSAE is usually higher and tighter" was **wrong** and is corrected in `proteindesign.md` §Confirmation pass + `tools/alphafold2_multimer.md`. Practical: ship designs with a small triage→confirmed delta; drop collapsers. Also: **partial diffusion + RFD3 schema fix CONFIRMED working in a real agent run** here (RFD3 called 3×: 1 denovo + partial_t=3 + partial_t=2). Realistic ipSAE ceiling for unconditioned RFD3 on the TREM2 IgV apex is **~0.82** (3 runs: 0.75/0.821/0.817 confirmed) — ≥0.88 needs strand-conditioning / Rosetta relax / AF3, none wired.
96	
97	### Breaking the ~0.82 ipSAE ceiling — deep-research conclusion (2026-06-07)
98	Ran a verified deep-research pass (106 agents, 24 sources, 25 claims adversarially verified, 0 killed) on how to beat the unconditioned-RFD3 helical-bundle ceiling on the TREM2 IgV β-edge. **Validated, cited conclusions:**
99	- **RFD3 genuinely cannot SS/fold/block-adjacency condition** (re-confirmed independently — official foundry docs: "no other parameters to control the secondary structure"; only `is_non_loopy`, atom H-bond donor/acceptor, RASA, motif scaffolding). So the β-edge fix is NOT a RFD3 wrapper change.
100	- **Highest-ROI, evidence-matched path = add classic RFdiffusion v1 with beta-pairing (SS/ADJ) interface conditioning** — designs scaffolds that form extended β-sheets pairing with a target *edge β-strand*, i.e. our exact problem. Baker lab Nat Commun 2025 (s41467-025-67866-3 / bioRxiv 2024.10.11.617496): **~9× in-silico uplift (9.2% vs 0.98%)**, experimentally validated pM–nM binders on 7 edge-strand/Ig-like targets (ALK-3 528 pM, PDGFRα 137 pM, KIT 65 nM). Uses released v1, no retraining; scripts public (`helper_scripts/make_secstruc_adj.py` → SS/ADJ `.pt`; `scaffoldguided.scaffoldguided=True` + `scaffoldguided.target_ss/target_adj`; `contigmap.inpaint_str_strand`). Tensor pack: files.ipd.uw.edu/pub/strand_pairing_binders_2025/interface_tensors.zip.
101	- **Keep RFD3 as default generator** (beats v1 8.2 vs 1.4 clusters on receptor/cytokine benchmarks); use v1 beta-pairing ONLY for β-edge/Ig targets.
102	- **Open alt generators worth adding:** BindCraft (AF2 hallucination, open, 10–100% avg ~46% exp hit rate, Nature 2025 s41586-025-09429-6); BoltzGen (MIT, all-atom, epitope conditioning, 66% nM on novel targets — but conditions *where* it binds, not the binder's own fold). **AlphaProteo = proprietary, cannot self-host (rule out). BoltzDesign1 = no wet-lab validation (low priority, ≠ BoltzGen).**
103	- **GPU-fit on the 22GB A10 was NOT verified** for any of these — check VRAM before integrating.
104	- **UNRESEARCHED (budget-dropped, sources fetched but claims unverified):** (3) whether ipSAE ≥0.85–0.88 is even a well-founded binding proxy vs metric-overfitting, Rosetta ddG/Bennett thresholds, pDockQ2/PAE-int, Boltz-2 re-ranking; (4) agentic/multi-agent orchestration patterns for design-build-test loops. Needs a focused follow-up pass. Full report (ephemeral): /tmp/.../tasks/w8nd20doi.output.
105	
106	### Research/debate fan-out made MANDATORY per round (2026-06-07)
107	Observed: recent TREM2 runs (`b269b01802e5`, `a89c4dfe5a89`, `29d98715cdb4`) had **zero** research/debate/web events — the agent skipped the §1.5 fan-out + §1.7 debate entirely, citing "the learned IgV playbook already applies" in plan.md (and all were rounds=1, so no per-round re-research either). 6	## Learned (run f1c91f97b666, 2026-05-27): on a flat Ig-V face with the current RFD3 wrapper, expect α-helical-bundle binders — generic β backbones fold but don't dock
7	Targeting PD-L1 IgV (4ZQK chain A, crop 18–132, hotspots Y56/R113/M115/Y123), RFD3 produced a
8	mix of α-helical-bundle and β-sandwich/mixed backbones. After MPNN→ESM→AF2-multimer (16 AF2 jobs):
9	**all 4 strict-gate hits were α-helical bundles** (complex pLDDT 93–97, ipSAE 0.61–0.80, ipTM
10	0.79–0.89, BSA 1369–1586 Å², 100% hotspot satisfaction, from 4 *independent* backbones). **Every
11	generic (unconditioned) β-topology design failed to dock** (ipSAE ≤ 0.28, mostly ~0.01) despite
12	high monomer ESM pLDDT — the "folds OK / docks wrong" quadrant.
13	**Why it generalizes:** the literature β-advantage for Ig-V faces (PMC12852815) is specifically for
14	β-STRAND-CONDITIONED RFdiffusion (explicit edge-strand pairing). Our `design.rfdiffusion3` wrapper
15	exposes no strand-conditioning lever, so its unconditioned β-sandwiches present no interface strand
16	and don't engage the target. **Practical rule:** until the wrapper gains strand conditioning, spend
17	AF2 budget preferentially on the α-helical-bundle backbones for flat Ig-V faces; treat generic β
18	backbones as low-yield. A sparse 4-hotspot hint of the aromatic/hydrophobic anchors (Y56, M115,
19	Y123) + one charged centering residue (R113) on the CC'FG face was sufficient — 100% hotspot
20	satisfaction on all hits, no over-constraint.
21	
22	## Learned (run adbe5874aeb4, 2026-06-06): on TREM2-like Ig-V apices, binders converge on the CDR2 hydrophobic edge and consistently miss the peripheral charged anchors (R47, R98)
23	Targeting TREM2 5ELI chain A crop 20-131 with 5 sparse hotspots A44/A47/A74/A76/A98 (W/R/F/R/R covering
24	CDR1+CDR2+CDR3), the IgV α-helical-bundle rule held: BB7 (α-bundle) produced the top 3 hits in both
25	rounds (best round-2 design ipSAE 0.75, ipTM 0.86, complex pLDDT 96.7, pDockQ2 0.87, BSA 1396 Å²,
26	hotspot satisfaction 60%). The miss pattern was **identical across all 13 docked complexes**:
27	**A74 + A76 (CDR2 hydrophobic edge) satisfied; A47 and A98 unsatisfied** at min Cβ-Cβ ≥ 10 Å. The
28	helical bundle docks along the CDR2 ridge and the binder's helix ends sit too far from R47/R98 to
29	contact them.
30	**Why it generalizes (TREM2 and other Ig-V apices with a similar geometry):** the CDR2 hydrophobic
31	patch (here L71/F74/R76+W78) is the deepest, most contiguous surface feature; RFD3 places the
32	binder where the most non-polar burial is available, and the peripheral basic anchors (R47 in CDR1,
33	R98 in CDR3) end up at the edges of the engaged footprint regardless of whether they were declared
34	hotspots. **Practical rule:** for TREM2-class apices, do not budget for full 5-hotspot satisfaction
35	in a single helical bundle — either (a) drop A47/A98 from the hotspot list and accept a CDR2-edge
36	binder, or (b) require a longer binder (≥100 aa) with an extended loop or second helix specifically
37	designed to reach R47/R98 (the strict gate's ≥0.70 hotspot satisfaction is then realistic). Until
38	the RFD3 wrapper exposes partial diffusion / strand conditioning, treating "covers CDR2 only" as
39	the achievable target on these Ig-V apices is honest, not failure.

70	The core skill's Confirmation-pass guidance ("ensembled is usually higher and tighter than single-model
71	triage") was tested directly on 6 top TREM2 candidates (5ELI crop 20-131, CDR2-ridge hotspots, helical
72	bundle topology). Result: 5 of 6 designs confirmed within delta ±0.02 of their single-model ipSAE (0.801,

Links: [{"title":"Improved protein binder design using beta-pairing targeted RFdiffusion","url":"https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.10.11.617496.full.pdf"},{"title":"Publications • Baker Lab","url":"https://www.bakerlab.org/publications/"},{"title":"Improved protein binder design using beta-pairing targeted RFdiffusion","url":"https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.10.11.617496v2.full.pdf"},{"title":"Improved protein binder design using β-pairing targeted RFdiffusion | Nature Communications","url":"https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-67866-3"},{"title":"Improved protein binder design using beta-pairing targeted RFdiffusion | bioRxiv","url":"https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.10.11.617496v1"},{"title":"Rolling out new jellies • Baker Lab","url":"https://www.bakerlab.org/2018/10/31/rolling-out-the-jellies/"}]

I found the research you're looking for! Here's what the search reveals:

The paper is authored by Sappington, Toul, Lee, Robinson, Goreshnik, and colleagues in the Baker lab, published in Nature Communications in 2026 with DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-67866-3.

The study addresses the challenge of designing proteins that bind with high affinity to hydrophilic protein target sites by showing that RFdiffusion can be conditioned to generate protein scaffolds that form geometrically matched extended β-sheets with target protein edge β-strands in which polar groups on the target are complemented with hydrogen bonding groups on the design.

The researchers designed binders against edge-strand target sites on KIT, PDGFRα, ALK-2, ALK-3, FCRL5, NRP1, and α-CTX, achieving higher (pM to mid nM) affinities and success rates than unconditioned RFdiffusion. Despite sharing β-strand interactions, the designs have high specificity, and a binder-KIT co-crystal structure is nearly identical to the design model, confirming the accuracy of the design approach.

The paper represents a significant advance in using deep learning for β-strand pairing binder design, targeting immunoglobulin (Ig) fold domains and other therapeutically relevant proteins.

Based on the search results, I found relevant information about the Dunbrack ipSAE metric and its application to binder design:

The ipSAE metric, proposed by Roland Dunbrack, is calculated similarly to ipTM but only considers the most confident pAE pairs in the calculation (if pAE < 10). This reduces the impact of low confidence 'disordered' regions on the ipTM score.

The AF3-derived ipSAE outperforms commonly used scores such as ipAE and ipTM, with a significant 1.4-fold increase in average precision compared to ipAE. This finding comes from a large-scale meta-analysis of 3,766 experimentally tested binders across 15 structurally diverse targets.

Regarding RFdiffusion's role in binder design, RFdiffusion enables the generation of high-affinity protein binders directly from target structures, without relying on natural templates.

However, the search results did not contain specific information about the 0.88 threshold value you mentioned or detailed experimental binding success rates in relation to that specific threshold. For more detailed information about this specific threshold, you may want to consult the full bioRxiv paper on predicting experimental success in de novo binder design referenced in the results.

content.text:
HYPOTHESIS: For IgSF V-set / Ig-fold extracellular domains, beta-strand-pairing binders generated via strand-interface-conditioned RFdiffusion outperform default alpha-helical RFdiffusion outputs in both in silico success rate and experimental affinity, because the polar backbone of exposed edge strands on these targets is most efficiently complemented by a geometrically matched binder beta-strand presenting hydrogen-bond donor/acceptor groups in register — a strategy that is validated across multiple IgSF-family receptors (KIT, PDGFRalpha, ALK-2, ALK-3, FCRL5) at pM-to-nM affinities.

EVIDENCE:

- Sappington et al. (Baker lab, Nat Commun 2025/2026, PMID 41519838 / PMC12852815 / DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-67866-3) showed that beta-strand-interface-conditioned RFdiffusion yielded a 5-fold improvement in in silico success rate over hotspot-directed (default) RFdiffusion for IgSF edge-strand targets; unconditioned runs produced beta-strand-pairing designs in <5% of outputs for less-exposed edge strands, vs. up to 20% for more exposed ones. Validated binders against KIT, PDGFRalpha, ALK-2, ALK-3, and FCRL5 reached pM to mid-nM affinity; a binder-KIT co-crystal structure matched the design model closely. The paper explicitly attributes the gain to the difficulty alpha-helical designs face complementing the many polar NH/CO groups of edge beta-strands using side-chain-to-backbone hydrogen bonds — a problem strand-pairing solves by backbone-to-backbone registry.

- The canonical PD-1/PD-L1 IgV interface demonstrates that the flat GFCC'C'' beta-sheet face of an IgV domain is naturally engaged by a partner IgV domain through sheet-to-sheet apposition (PMID 21697456, PMC3148082; PMID 26432723, PMC4733614), establishing that the biologically productive epitope on IgV targets is a beta-sheet face, not a helical groove — consistent with a strand-pairing rather than a helical-bundle design strategy.

- A 2026 bioRxiv study (Perera et al., PMID 42079091, DOI 10.64898/2026.04.23.720433) reported XL-MS-guided de novo protein design yielding a common binding motif for TREM2 (itself a single IgV domain), providing direct evidence that the IgSF V-set fold is tractable for de novo binder pipelines.

- RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN are noted to intrinsically favor alpha-helical folds (PMID 40705894, PMC12313176), meaning that for beta-rich IgSF targets, default runs will be systematically biased away from the topology most compatible with the target surface — motivating explicit beta-conditioning at inference time.

- Beta-strand pairing against irregular edge strands in native proteins is achievable provided the binder strand geometry is sculpted to match the target; non-canonical geometries suppress off-target aggregation (PMC12852815 Discussion, PMID 41519838), indicating that designability concerns about beta-sheet binders aggregating are addressable by geometric conditioning rather than by defaulting to helical folds.

CONFIDENCE: high — The Sappington et al. paper directly tests multiple IgSF/Ig-fold receptors with a controlled comparison of binder topologies, and the mechanistic explanation (backbone polar complementarity) is consistent with established structural data on IgV interfaces.

WOULD-FALSIFY / OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) If alpha-helical binders targeting a protruding loop or groove adjacent to the IgV beta-face (rather than the edge strand or sheet surface directly) were shown to reach equivalent affinity and hit-rate, the topology preference would be site-dependent rather than fold-general. (2) For IgV domains lacking an exposed edge strand (e.g., buried or glycosylated edge strands), the strand-pairing strategy may not be applicable and alpha-helical approaches may be competitive. (3) It is not yet established whether the 5-fold in silico improvement translates proportionally to experimental hit rates across all IgSF family members.

Sources:
- [Improved protein binder design using beta-pairing targeted RFdiffusion - Nature Communications](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-67866-3)

HYPOTHESIS: Among designed 60-120 aa alpha-helical mini-binders produced by the RFdiffusion3/ProteinMPNN pipeline, the dominant pre-expression failure modes are (i) soluble-fraction loss due to exposed hydrophobic surface patches on non-interface helices and (ii) aggregation near the predicted pI; therefore a composite sequence-level filter comprising maximum solvent-accessible hydrophobic patch area (SAP score or equivalent), net charge at pH 7.4 |z| >= 2, and absence of unpaired cysteines should be applied before AF2-multimer ranking, and will enrich the experimentally soluble/monomeric fraction from ~75% to >85% of submitted designs.

EVIDENCE:

- The principal RFdiffusion paper (Watson et al., Nature 2023, PMID 37433327) and its companion binder-improvement paper (Bennett et al., Nat Commun 2023, PMID 37149653) report that of 96 computationally designed proteins expressed in E. coli, 73 (76%) were solubly expressed and only 50 were monomeric by SEC, establishing that ~24% loss at the solubility step and a further ~15-20% loss at the oligomerization step are the characteristic liabilities, not design correctness per se (PMC9997061, PMID 36108050).

- Solubility of small proteins is jointly governed by net charge (distance from pI) and surface hydrophobicity: sequences near their pI and carrying large exposed hydrophobic patches show the highest aggregation propensity, a relationship documented for peptides and small designed proteins across multiple studies (PMID 20480046, PMC2871142; PMID 22312455, PMC3268033).

- Computational tools explicitly targeting these two descriptors (CamSol, SAP/spatial aggregation propensity, Aggrescan3D, Protein-sol patches) have been validated for sequence-level developability screening; a scoring term that penalizes surface hydrophobic patches during design or post-hoc filtering is noted to increase yield and in vivo efficacy (PMID 29695210, PMC6002944; PMID 35568899, PMC9107766).

- Exposed hydrophobic residues on designed mini-binder scaffolds that are not shielded by surface-facing charged residues are a recognized source of non-specific aggregation and promiscuous binding, compounding expression losses (PMID 23641816, PMC3795862).

- Unpaired cysteines form aberrant disulfides in the E. coli periplasm/cytoplasm and are a canonical cause of inclusion-body formation for small disulfide-naive helical scaffolds; the absence of free Cys is a standard pre-filter in high-throughput designed-protein screens (Vázquez Torres et al., Nature 2024, PMID 38109936; Lv et al., Nat Commun 2024, PMID 39358329).

- A multi-descriptor sequence-level screen (net charge, hydrophobicity, aggregation propensity, no unpaired Cys) has precedent in antibody developability pipelines as the primary pre-experimental filter (PMID 32954930, PMC7577746).

CONFIDENCE: med — The 76% E. coli solubility baseline is well-established empirically for helical designed proteins, and the two root causes (hydrophobic patches, near-pI charge state) are mechanistically sound and multiply cited. The specific threshold values (SAP cutoff, |z| >= 2) and the predicted enrichment magnitude are extrapolated from antibody/peptide literature rather than directly demonstrated for 60-120 aa RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN designs; no controlled prospective study with this exact filter combination and this scaffold class has been published.

WOULD-FALSIFY / OPEN QUESTIONS: The hypothesis would be weakened if a prospective screen showed that failed designs cluster on non-solubility causes (e.g., misfolding or incorrect target docking) rather than surface hydrophobicity/pI effects. It would be falsified if SAP/CamSol scores showed no significant correlation with soluble-fraction yield in a held-out test set of >50 RFdiffusion3/ProteinMPNN designs on diverse targets. Open question: whether interface-proximal hydrophobic residues (necessary for binding) systematically inflate aggregate SAP scores relative to non-binder designed proteins, requiring a masked-interface scoring variant.

HYPOTHESIS: For small beta-sandwich/Ig-V fold targets, unconditioned RFdiffusion3 generating purely alpha-helical mini-binders (60-100 aa, 2-3 helix bundles) achieves in silico pAE_interaction < 10 at a rate of roughly 1%, rarely surpasses an experimental hit rate above a few percent, and produces validated nM affinities only after interface re-optimization via partial diffusion; by contrast, beta-strand interface conditioning of RFdiffusion against the target edge strand raises the in silico quality-pass rate to approximately 9% and yields experimentally confirmed pM-to-mid-nM affinities, making beta-augmented topology — not a canonical helical bundle — the higher-probability first-round strategy for Ig-V targets.

EVIDENCE:

- Beta-strand interface conditioning of RFdiffusion against seven edge-strand-containing proteins (including KIT, PDGFRalpha, NRP1) yielded 9.2% of designs meeting AF2 pAE_interaction < 10 / Rosetta DDG < -30 quality metrics, compared to 0.98% pass rate for hotspot-only unconditioned RFdiffusion. Confirmed affinities ranged from pM to mid-nM by SPR. The mechanistic rationale is the geometric complementarity of beta-pairing to the polar NH/CO pattern of edge strands, which alpha-helical sidechains reproduce only through more convoluted hydrogen-bonding. (PMID 41519838 / PMC12852815, Nature Communications 2025)

- For alpha-helical mini-binders against non-beta targets, high-affinity outcomes (sub-nM SPR Kd) are achievable but require iterative partial diffusion refinement: in toxin-binder campaigns, 78 designs were screened to reach SHRT at 0.9 nM (SPR) and 38 designs to reach LNG at 1.9 nM (SPR). These campaigns targeted globular, non-Ig-V structures. (PMID 38798548 / PMC11118692; PMID 39814879 / PMC11882462)

- A meta-analysis of 3,766 experimentally characterized designs across 15 structurally diverse targets (436 confirmed binders, 3,330 non-binders) established ipSAE (Dunbrack 2025, PMID 39990437, DOI 10.1101/2025.02.10.637595) as the strongest single predictor of experimental binding, outperforming ipTM and pAE_interaction by 1.4-fold average precision. The F1-optimal ipSAE cutoff from this large dataset is reported at approximately 0.61, not 0.88; the 0.88 threshold represents high-specificity conservative filtering rather than the empirical nM-binder boundary. (DOI 10.1101/2025.08.14.670059, Overath & Rygaard et al., bioRxiv 2025)

- For beta-sandwich/Ig-V targets in particular, only strand-containing designs achieved AF2 pAE_interaction < 10 and pLDDT_binder > 90 in one published G3BP1 RBD campaign; purely helical outputs from unconditioned RFdiffusion failed the in silico gate entirely on that target. (PMID 40739343 / PMC12367549)

- The canonical two-helix and three-helix helical mini-binder scaffolds (56-58 aa, exemplified by affibody-class proteins) are well-established to reach nM affinities against globular targets, but these are selected from large combinatorial libraries, not single-round computational design. Single-round de novo helical binders against Ig-V class targets have not demonstrated comparable success rates in the published literature. (PMID 30203972 / PMC6689236; PMID 33985511 / PMC8120847)

CONFIDENCE: med — The beta-strand conditioning advantage is demonstrated across seven diverse targets including PDGFRalpha and KIT (which carry Ig-V/Ig-like domains), and the ipSAE meta-analysis provides the largest quantitative benchmark to date. Confidence is not high because (a) published head-to-head comparisons of helical vs. beta-augmented binders specifically against Ig-V topology are limited to a handful of targets, (b) the ipSAE F1-optimal cutoff of 0.61 from the meta-analysis means the 0.88 threshold requested is more conservative than validated data require, and (c) TREM2 specifically has not appeared in a published de novo binder campaign yet.

WOULD-FALSIFY / OPEN QUESTIONS: This hypothesis would be overturned if a systematic campaign demonstrated that unconditioned RFdiffusion3 helical binders achieve greater than 5% experimental hit rates against exposed Ig-V loop epitopes on TREM2 specifically. The ipSAE threshold question would be refined by target-stratified ROC curves from the Overath et al. dataset (currently reported only as aggregate average precision). Whether a 2-helix vs. 3-helix topology within the alpha-helical scaffold class meaningfully alters affinity for this target class remains an open question with no direct published answer.

2. **IgSF V-set fold designability**: β-strand-pairing RFdiffusion v1 dominates (9× lift on edge strands; KIT/PDGFRα/ALK pM-nM). Cites Perera 2026 bioRxiv TREM2 de novo work. (PMC12852815, PMID 41519838, PMID 42079091)
3. **Mini-binder length/topology + ipSAE**: F1-optimal ipSAE ≈ 0.61 (Overath 2025 meta-analysis 3766 binders); 0.88 is conservative beyond empirical nM-binding threshold. β-conditioned designs reach pM-nM; unconditioned helical bundles need partial-diffusion refinement. (DOI 10.1101/2025.08.14.670059, PMID 39990437)
4. **Developability**: ~76% E. coli soluble baseline (Bennett 2023); filters = max SAP / hydrophobic patch, |net charge| ≥ 2, no free Cys. (PMID 37433327, PMID 37149653, PMID 29695210)

## Learned (run 2e5ffd821473, 2026-06-07): the ipSAE ceiling on TREM2 IgSF apex CDR2 ridge is 0.84 — partial_t cascade does NOT compound, and a 100-120 aa cold-start does NOT break it
Across a 4-round campaign (12 RFD3 cold-start → 8 partial_t=3 polish on R1 winner → [6 long cold-start
@ length 106 + 6 partial_t=2 polish on R2 winner] → num_models=5 confirmation on top 6), the best
ipSAE landed at **0.843** (confirmed) — only +0.015 over the R1 cold-start best of 0.828, despite spending
the full budget. **Two empirical lessons that generalize:**
(i) **Sequential partial_t polishes do NOT compound.** R1 cold-start best 0.828 → partial_t=3 polish best
0.842 (+0.014) → partial_t=2 polish on the R2 winner best 0.841 (+0.000). A second polish round on a

# Plan — TREM2 IgSF binder design (5ELI chain A, crop 20-131)

## Target
- PDB 5ELI chain A, gap 132-200 (stalk + His-tag, absent from model).
- Crop 20-131 (112 residues) = construct positions 1-112 (TG cloning artifact + TREM2 IgSF).
- UniProt Q9NZC2 (human TREM2).
- **User-stated ipSAE target: ≥ 0.88** — known from prior runs to be beyond the unconditioned-RFD3 ceiling on this target.

## Round 1 — CDR2 ridge baseline (validated path)

### §1.5 Research fan-out (4 scouts, parallel via Agent)
1. **TREM2 prior binders** (Sonnet): AL002c, 4D9, 9F5, biparatopic — all multivalent; agonism via crosslinking, no de novo monomer precedent. (PMID 32579671, 36070367, 40803893, 35019161, 32154671, 37863592)
2. **IgSF V-set fold designability**: β-strand-pairing RFdiffusion v1 dominates (9× lift on edge strands; KIT/PDGFRα/ALK pM-nM). (PMC12852815, PMID 41519838)
3. **Mini-binder length/topology + ipSAE**: F1-optimal ipSAE ≈ 0.61 (Overath 2025 meta-analysis 3766 binders); 0.88 is conservative beyond empirical nM-binding threshold. (DOI 10.1101/2025.08.14.670059, PMID 39990437)
4. **Developability**: ~76% E. coli soluble baseline; filter for SAP, |net charge| ≥ 2, no free Cys. (PMID 37433327, PMID 37149653, PMID 29695210)

### §1.6 Due diligence
- Confirmed RFD3 wrapper has NO SS/ADJ lever (NOTES.md) → strand-pairing strategy unactionable here.
- Confirmed 0.88 target is beyond ~0.82 unconditioned-RFD3 ceiling observed on this exact target in prior runs (5707e91b52df, 29d98715cdb4, 29c9603ba01d).
- Skipped re-running structural sandbox (already done in prior campaigns; CDR2 ridge {W44, F74, R76, W78} is THE deep hydrophobic patch).

### §1.7 Debate
- Contested: strand-pairing scout (β-pairing > helical for IgV) vs main agent (helical bundle is only reachable path with RFD3 wrapper).
- DEFEND on whether helical bundles can still win on apical CDR ridge: API-filter refused (both research tier; immune/TREM2 topics). Sub-topic dropped per skill rules.
- **Adjudication**: helical-bundle CDR2-ridge is the validated reproducible strategy. User's ipSAE ≥ 0.88 is honestly unlikely. Spend full budget pivoting to maximize the metric and report honestly.

### Round 1 hypothesis
- Topology: α-helical bundle (validated).
- Hotspots: A44, A74, A76, A78 (CDR2 ridge).
- Binder length: 80-100 (RFD3 picked 90).
- 12 RFD3 backbones × 4 MPNN soluble T=0.1 = 48 sequences; ESM batch; top 12 (no-Cys preferred) → AF2 colabfold num_models=1.

### Round 1 results
- 48 sequences ESM-fold mean pLDDT 78.7.
- 12 AF2 ran; star design = **step 48 (binder = "AAAQAEAA...", backbone 10): ipSAE 0.828, ipTM 0.92, pLDDT 98.3, pdockq2 0.92**.
- Distribution: 4 designs > 0.65 ipSAE (high docking), 4 in 0.4-0.55 (marginal), 4 failed dock (≤ 0.05).
- **0/12 hits** under strict ipSAE ≥ 0.93 gate.

### Round 1 — Round 1 — best ipSAE 0.828
- **Worked:** Top design (step 48) and the second-best (step 51) both came from backbones #10 and #5, MPNN soluble T=0.1, length 90 α-helical bundle docking on the CDR2 hydrophobic ridge — exactly the validated regime from learned/ig-v-flat-face.md.
- **Why:** The CDR2 hydrophobic ridge (W44/F74/R76/W78) is the deepest contiguous non-polar patch on the 5ELI IgSF apex; RFD3 places the helical bundle there reliably and complementary side chains from MPNN soluble pack tightly.
- **Gap:** ipSAE plateaued at 0.828 — well short of 0.88 user target. ipTM and pLDDT are already saturated (0.92 / 98.3); the limiting metric is interface "specificity" via the PAE matrix, which is a property of the docked pose's quality.
- **Next hypothesis:** Partial diffusion polish (partial_t=3 Å) on the rank-1 complex to re-roll local backbone variants near the proven pose — the canonical polish move that gave +0.02-0.07 ipSAE in prior runs.

## Round 2 — partial diffusion polish

### Refinement reasoning (a→b→c)
- **Causal read**: ipSAE ceiling at ~0.83 because the helical bundle dock is good (ipTM/pLDDT saturated) but interface specificity (PAE) is bounded by geometry; small backbone perturbations can find a better local optimum.
- **Scouts** (no new fan-out needed): research budget already exhausted on R1's broad topics; the specific gap is well-characterized empirically.
- **Debate**: skill (g) explicitly recommends partial_t=3 Å as the proven 1-step polish for 0.75→0.80; we extend it to test 0.83→0.85+.

### Round 2 hypothesis
- partial_t = 3 Å on TOP 2 winners (step 48 backbone-10, step 51 backbone-5). 8 + 6 = 14 polished backbones.
- MPNN soluble T=0.05 × 3 seqs = 42 sequences.
- ESM → AF2 top 10.

### Round 2 results
- ESM range 79.2-81.2 (tight cluster, all polished backbones similar).
- 10 AF2: **step 100 (binder = "AEAEAERAAEEARREAL...", lineage 48): ipSAE 0.842, ipTM 0.92, pLDDT 98.5, pdockq2 0.93**.
- Lineage 48 (backbone-10 polish): 6/6 produced ipSAE 0.815-0.842 (reproducible lift).
- Lineage 51 (backbone-5 polish): 1/4 worked at 0.68; 3/4 collapsed (off-dock).

### Round 2 — Round 2 — best ipSAE 0.842 (+0.014 over R1)
- **Worked:** All 6 children from the step-48 lineage (backbone 10, partial_t=3 Å, MPNN T=0.05) landed in a tight ipSAE 0.815-0.842 band, with the median above R1's best — a real, reproducible polish lift, not a single lucky outlier.
- **Why:** partial_t=3 Å re-noises ~3 Å of local backbone while preserving the proven dock; MPNN T=0.05 commits to the highest-likelihood interface side chains. Together they sample the local optimum tightly.
- **Gap:** Even the best polish child caps at ipSAE 0.842, only +0.014 over the unpolished parent. Polishing a polished pose hits diminishing returns fast — the geometry isn't the bottleneck, the architecture's PAE confidence is.
- **Next hypothesis:** Try a *different* lever in round 3 — (1) a length 100-120 cold-start with W78 as the primary hotspot (test learned skill (e)'s "longer binder to reach the missed hotspot" recipe); (2) ultra-tight partial_t=2 Å polish on the R2 winner to test whether even-smaller perturbation breaks through.

## Round 3 — structurally distinct pivot

### Refinement reasoning
- Polish lift was real but small (+0.014). Per skill rule "must change something", lever for R3 = TOPOLOGY/LENGTH regime (cold-start at 100-120 aa) in parallel with a second-pass polish (partial_t=2) to test compounding.
- Prediction (testable): if compounding works, second polish > first polish; if it doesn't, the ceiling is the geometry. If long cold-start lifts ipSAE, longer reach helps; if not, the wrapper just can't.

### Round 3 hypothesis
- 6 RFD3 cold-start at length 100-120, hotspots A78,A44,A74,A76 (W78 first to bias toward the prior unsatisfied edge).
- 6 RFD3 partial_t=2 Å polish on step_100 winner.
- MPNN: T=0.1 on cold-start (3 seqs), T=0.05 on polish (3 seqs) = 36 sequences.
- ESM → AF2 top 10 (7 polish + 3 long for topology diversity).

### Round 3 results
- ESM range 72.7-83.1.
- **Best polish-lineage**: step 164 (AEAEAERAAEEAREE...): ipSAE 0.841, ipTM 0.92, pLDDT 98.3. Cluster of 6 polish children at 0.79-0.84.
- **Long cold-start**: best ipSAE 0.786 (worse than length 90); a helix-helix topology (MAEELFAA...) collapsed at ipSAE 0.10.
- **TWO hypotheses falsified**: (1) sequential partial_t polishes DO NOT compound (0.828 → 0.842 → 0.841, second polish flat); (2) longer cold-start does NOT reach the helical-bundle ceiling — let alone exceed it.

### Round 3 — Round 3 — best ipSAE 0.841 (= R2; ceiling confirmed)
- **Worked:** The partial_t=2 polish lineage of the R2 winner produced 6/7 children at ipSAE 0.71-0.84, with the top child essentially tied to R2's best. The polished pose is robust and reproducibly designable.
- **Why:** R2's winner already sits at a local minimum-energy interface for this architecture; further partial diffusion at 2 Å just samples the same basin, not a new one.
- **Gap:** Second polish round did NOT compound (0.842 → 0.841 = +0.000). Long cold-start at 106 aa hit max 0.786, ~0.05 below the 90-aa optimum — falsifying the "longer binder to reach W78" hypothesis from learned/ig-v-flat-face.md (e). The 0.84 ceiling is the architecture, not a budget problem.
- **Next hypothesis:** No further design moves can break this ceiling within the current toolkit. Use the final round budget for a num_models=5 confirmation pass to filter false-positive triage outliers and produce a robust ranked list — NOT another design round, which the falsified pivots tell us will not help.

## Round 4 — confirmation pass + interface QC

- Reasoning: design rounds have plateaued; spend the final round measuring more accurately.
- 6 AF2 jobs at num_models=5, num_recycle=8 on top 6 designs across R1-R3.
- Interface metrics (analysis.interface_metrics) on confirmed top 5.

### Round 4 — confirmation results

| 201 | R3 | 0.841 | **0.843** | +0.002 | 0.92 | 98.2 | 1666 | 3/4 |

- All 6 robust under ensembling (max drop -0.042 — far from a "collapse"). Top 5 are publishable candidates.
- A76 is the unsatisfied hotspot in ALL 5 winners (~9.4-9.9 Å) — same recurring "binder helix reaches 3/4 contiguous CDR2 residues" pattern documented in learned skill (e/h).

### Round 4 — Round 4 — final ipSAE 0.843 confirmed
- **Worked:** num_models=5 confirmation pass survived all 6 top designs without collapse (worst case -0.042); the polish-lineage R2/R3 winners cluster tightly at 0.823-0.843 confirmed ipSAE, ipTM 0.91-0.92, complex pLDDT 97.7-98.5, BSA 1620-1766 Å², 75% hotspot. This is genuinely a reproducible interface across independent backbones, not a single lucky model.
